item.title: Indian Teacher Rouble Nagi Wins $1 Million Global Teacher Prize
item.description: Rouble Nagi, an Indian teacher and social activist, has been awarded the prestigious $1 million Global Teacher Prize at the World Governments Summit in Dubai. This award recognises outstanding educators whose impact goes beyond traditional classrooms and into communities that often lack access to formal schooling. item.title: Iran Formally Allows Women To Get Motorcycle Licenses; Yes, In 2026
item.description: When a government “allows” women to ride a motorcycle, you know freedom was never the point. In most countries, riding a motorcycle is forgettable. item.title: 'The Renewal Years': How Japan Rethinks Menopause Through Nutrition And Care
item.description: In Japan, menopause is known as konenki, a term that translates to “the turning point of life energy.” It is not framed as decline or loss, but as a shift, like a period, where the body recalibrates, and a woman steps into a new phase of strength, perspective, and authority. item.title: A Tiny Piece Of Cloth Can Be A Life-Saver: Sanjeevani’s 'Pink Tag Project' Shows How
item.description: In a village outside Delhi, a woman notices a Pink Tag stitched inside her blouse- next to the wash-care label. It gently reminds her how to check herself with simple visuals, no alarms, no fear, just awareness. This is how the Network 18 Sanjeevani - Pink Tag Project, born in rural India, is being amplified by local tailors and community trust.
